  mappings:

This example uses macros, named operators, and paired delimiters. Render it with
either MathJax or KaTeX; the same style file supplies the declarations.

## Macros and optional defaults

The first argument of `\shifted` defaults to `x`:

$$\shifted{y} \qquad \shifted[z]{y}$$

The `labelstyle: mathsf` mapping explicitly chooses the appearance of a label.
Mappings are ordinary aliases, so they can use names chosen for your own notation:

$$\vectorspace{V}$$

## Operators and delimiters

The starred operator declaration gives its subscript limits-style placement:

$$\best_{v\in V} f(v)$$

Paired delimiters support fixed, automatic, and explicit sizing:

$$\bracketpair{u}{v} \qquad \bracketpair*{\frac{u}{2}}{v} \qquad \bracketpair[\Big]{u}{v}$$

## Renderer vocabulary

These commands come from the renderer, without declarations in the style file:

$$\boldsymbol{x} \xleftrightarrow{T} \boldsymbol{y}$$

MathJax uses the same extension profile on every page, including `boldsymbol`
and `mathtools`. KaTeX uses its built-in vocabulary. Support for individual body
commands can differ between engines; successful declaration parsing alone does
not validate their mathematical contents.

For example, `\newcommand{\custom}{\unknownCommand{x}}` is a valid declaration
in the supported syntax, but using `\custom` would produce a renderer error.
Check representative formulas with each renderer before publishing.
